# definednet_domain_verification (Resource)

Verifies ownership of a `definednet_domain`. Create asks the API to look up the domain's TXT record and keeps retrying until it is found or the create timeout passes, so the record can be published by a DNS resource in the same configuration (use `depends_on`). Reference `domain_id` from this resource, not from the domain, in resources that need a verified domain so they are ordered after verification. The API has no un-verify, so destroying this resource only forgets it.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "definednet_domain_verification" "corp" {
  domain_id = definednet_domain.corp.id

  # The TXT record must exist before verification can succeed.
  depends_on = [cloudflare_dns_record.definednet_verification]

  timeouts {
    create = "15m"
  }
}

# Reference the verification, not the domain, so the provider is created
# only after the domain is verified.
resource "definednet_endpoint_oidc_provider" "okta" {
  # ...
  domain_id = definednet_domain_verification.corp.domain_id
  enabled   = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `domain_id` (String) ID of the `definednet_domain` to verify.

### Optional

- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Same as `domain_id`.

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) How long to keep retrying verification while the TXT record propagates. Defaults to `10m`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import definednet_domain_verification.corp domain-NFDI5G3RPXLHCPEXBVKEVLWPNI
```
